claim: CAS is an opt-in disk backend enabled with <metadata_type>content_addressed</metadata_type> that stores MergeTree part files once by content hash in a shared object-storage pool.

CAS coordination state, including refs, mount leases, and GC state, is stored in the object store; backend mutual exclusion relies on conditional PUT/DELETE (If-None-Match/If-Match) and startup probes fail closed.
The CAS implementation has a frontend layer, a backend-agnostic DB::Cas core, and a token-aware Cas::Backend seam; dependencies point inward and the core does not include the frontend.
A blob is identified by the pair BlobRef = (algo, digest), never by a bare digest, because multiple 16-byte hash algorithms can coexist.
Blob safety requires a fresh in-body incarnation_tag for every upload, a backend token, and exact-token deletion; resurrecting a condemned blob re-uploads from the writer's source with a fresh tag.
Per-table refs use an append-only log plus periodic snapshot, and CasRefStateMachine computes RefTableState = replay(snapshot, tail) for writers, recovery, GC intake, and fsck.

A regular GC round folds ref logs into source-edge in-degree runs, performs pre-CAS exact-token deletes of prior delete_pending entries, commits the round with one gc/state CAS, and performs cleanup after that CAS.
The blob body key family is blobs/<algo>/<S>/<hex>, with <algo> in ch128, xxh3, or sha256 and <S> equal to the first two hex characters.
Part manifests use keys shaped as cas/manifests/<ns>/<epoch>-<seq>/<NNNNNN>.proto and are immutable.
Ref transactions use immutable keys shaped as cas/refs/<ns>/_log/<txn_id>, while ref snapshots use immutable keys shaped as cas/refs/<ns>/_snap/<id>.proto.
A live ref resolving to an absent manifest or blob raises FILE_DOESNT_EXIST rather than producing a silent empty read.
Same-pool replica relinking transfers manifest information without blob bytes and requires matching content_addressed_pool_uuid; otherwise the receiver uses byte-fetch fallback.
The manifest decode cache assumes the backend token uniquely determines content, but the capability probe does not currently test TOKEN⟹CONTENT; a weak recycled token could serve stale manifests.
Plain-object helpers casPutObject and casRemoveObject bypass CasRequestController and can retry beyond the lease-bounded retry discipline used by the ref lane.
The isContentAddressed() whole-part transaction guard is duplicated across six MergeTree files, so a future caller that omits it could silently corrupt a CAS part.
The GC retention cursor can advance past a still-referenced generation before the best-effort hand-off delete; a crash in that window can leak the gc/gen/<g>/ prefix until fsck.
The current CAS code is described as the survivor of eras E0 through E4, ending in writer freshness metadata and the ref snapshot+log model; RootShardManifest was removed on 2026-07-12.
The archaeology report found no real-thread concurrency coverage beyond one single-flight test; other concurrency evidence is deterministic simulation, TLA+ models, and the external soak harness.
Content-addressed blobs are pool-global, while ref shards and manifests are scoped per server_root_id; dedup spans replicas at the blob level.
CAS is enabled per disk with metadata_type = content_addressed, and zero-copy replication remains available but is mutually exclusive with CAS per disk.
The hot/cold layout split changed GC discovery to GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/, making discovery proportional to ref shards rather than manifest backlog.
The @cas@ suffix on a table-directory segment marks the content-addressed boundary; detached refs use the same table namespace with a detached/ prefix.

A stable minted pool_uuid in _pool_meta is the same-pool criterion for fetch-by-relink; endpoint and prefix string matching is rejected because it can produce false-positive relinks and dangling refs.
Projection files are nested keys in the parent part's single manifest at paths such as <proj>.proj/<file>, rather than separate refs or sub-manifests.
Mutable integer blob refcounts were rejected in favor of an idempotent source-edge set folded from append-only +/- journal records.
The gc/registry namespace registry was removed because it grew monotonically, made GC cost proportional to namespaces ever created times root_shards, and did not reclaim empty shards.
A live ref must resolve through present keys; an absent key is a surfaced storage exception rather than a silent empty read (INV-NO-DANGLE).
Physical deletion requires a durable retire entry, fences at all root shards, a fold-through-fence zero-reachability recheck, and the exact observed token (INV-NO-LOSS).
Bucket versioning and versioning-suspended mode are rejected for the CA prefix because delete markers break the one-live-object model.
Every behavior-changing phase that changes deletion semantics or GC safety must have a GREEN TLA+ model before implementation begins; negative controls must violate their named invariants.
Each non-trivial implementation task uses a fresh implementer followed by independent specification and code-quality review subagents.
At soak checkpoints, both replicas must match an independent SQL model, ca-fsck must report dangling=0, and ca-gc-dryrun must propose only genuinely unreachable objects.
The D6 write-ahead lease-intent mechanism was removed because it created data-proportional persistent Keeper traffic and collided across writers building identical content.
The B140 dangle fix requires both build-root protection and fail-closed commit; the model found that either mechanism alone is insufficient.
CasStore owns mount lifecycle, ref snapshot+log state, manifest reads, and plain-object helpers; CasBuild owns blob hashing, staging, deduplication, and condemned resurrection.

Writable Store::open validates server_root_id, claims the owner, allocates a durable writer epoch, validates the CAS request budget, claims the mount lease, starts MountLeaseKeeper, and arms the mount fence.
A BlobDigest is a fixed 32-byte tail-zero value whose meaningful length is 16 bytes for ch128 and xxh3 and 32 bytes for sha256.
Strict CAS key parsers return std::nullopt for foreign or malformed keys rather than throwing.
The backend contract requires deleteExact to remove only the matching incarnation and requires TOKEN⟹CONTENT so a token match implies unchanged bytes for manifest cache reuse.
CasRequestController::putIfAbsentControlled gates every attempt by the fence and remaining deadline, resolves uncertain writes by exact GET, and treats differing existing bytes as CORRUPTED_DATA.
The TOKEN⟹CONTENT contract is load-bearing for the manifest cache but is not verified by Cas::Probe.
GC is leader-paced and one-pass: a stale leader may duplicate work but cannot roll back or mis-delete because operations are idempotent, monotone, or exact-token guarded.
A condemned blob has zero in-degree, an exact incarnation token observed by GC, a kCondemned sentinel row with source_id = 0, and Condemned per-blob metadata while its body may still exist.
A condemned entry becomes delete_pending only after surviving one full GC round and is deleted by the next pass with its exact token.
The GC fold uses a three-cursor streaming merge of prior edges, kCondemned rows, and current deltas, emitting at most one condemned sentinel per blob.
A crashed GC pass leaves only unadopted attempt-scoped artifacts; there is no crash-resume step, and later pruning reclaims those artifacts.

The GC scheduler uses gc_interval, gc_fold_threshold, gc_fold_max_defer_rounds, gc_snap_generations_to_keep, gc_shards, gc_meta_pool_size, mount_lease_ttl_ms, manifest_sweep_{list,delete}_budget_keys, and rebuild_edge_budget.
The GC hand-off can leak a whole generation if the process crashes after the retention cursor CAS and before the best-effort wholesale delete; a normal retry does not revisit the advanced cursor.
suppress_destructive is recomputed independently in fold and runRegularRound, so a future anomaly append between those reads could make fold and deletion decisions diverge.
The separate retired-set object family was removed in favor of kCondemned rows embedded in in-degree runs.
server_root_id must be a clean relative path without .., and two ClickHouse nodes must not share one server_root_id in the same pool.
The owner object at gc/server-roots/<srid>/owner rejects a foreign UUID and rejects re-claiming an absent owner over a non-empty data subtree with CORRUPTED_DATA.
writer_epoch is allocated from gc/server-roots/<srid>/epoch by a durable CAS bump and is strictly increasing across crashes and restarts.
A live mount lease stores MountLease{server_uuid, writer_epoch, hostname, pid, started_at_ms, seq, expires_at_ms, min_active, gc_fenced}.
The build watermark min_active is carried in the mount lease; the standalone watermark object and writer-side observed_gc_round retired-view machinery were removed.
MetaState::Clean means a blob is referenceable and MetaState::Condemned means GC has marked its in-degree zero; GC writes Condemned before deleting the body, and absent metadata is treated as live.
A part write proceeds as writeFile() × N followed by precommitAdd(), putBlob() × N, and promote().
The local scratch directory configured by local_scratch_path must hold one complete part's staged blobs, and temporary files are deleted after upload.
stageManifest writes the manifest with putIfAbsentStream before precommitAdd, and no blob body HEAD is required before the precommit CAS.
The revival invariant forbids reading a condemned or vanished blob to revive it; revival re-uploads the writer's own source bytes with a fresh incarnation.
The frontend translates IMetadataStorage and IMetadataTransaction path operations into (namespace, ref, file) routes and then into Cas::Store or Cas::Build operations.
CachedPartFolderAccess is a bounded validate-on-hit cache of immutable PartFolderView snapshots and uses single-flight cold builds.
The content_addressed factory defaults include gc_enabled=true, gc_interval_sec=60, root_shards=32, blob_hash=cityhash128, dedup_cache_bytes=64 MiB, and dedup_head_first_min_bytes=1 MiB.
server_root_id is required in the content-addressed disk configuration and is validated by Cas::validateServerRootId.
The factory configuration key gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes maps to the member gc_max_conditional_put_bytes_, dropping the s and making the member name misleading.
gc_scheduler is lazily created without a mutex in runOneGcRoundForTest and runGarbageCollectionRoundNow, so concurrent SYSTEM ... GC calls could race construction.
ContentAddressedTransaction::commit compensates for a mid-commit exception by best-effort dropping newly created refs and then rethrows.
ContentAddressedTransaction::unlinkFile deliberately no-ops for committed content files; a future caller that expects surgical committed-file deletion would silently retain the bytes.
moveDirectory publishes a CAS rename eagerly, outside the later transaction commit, to avoid holding MergeTree locks during object-store I/O.
Cross-namespace RENAME TABLE is non-atomic and can leave a table split across namespaces after a mid-loop exception; the operation is idempotent and re-drivable.
Part paths are classified using an Atomic UUID anchor or a non-Atomic part-directory fallback whose final three underscore groups are decimal.
DiskObjectStorage::prepareRead serves inline or mutable bytes from memory and uses the standard object-storage read pipeline plus a bounded FileView stage for blob payload windows.
The all-tree part-files design stores txn_version.txt, metadata_version.txt, and uuid.txt as ordinary entries in the part manifest rather than a separate ref sidecar.
The fold barrier treats a create-precommit as non-activating until its manifest body is present; once present, manifest expansion contributes the activating +1 blob edges.
Build::promote validates the manifest, checks the precommit owner, revalidates required blob leaves, and publishes the precommit-to-committed binding only after those checks.
Loose verbatim files use roots/<server>/<path>, while files inside a CAS archive use …@cas@/_files/<name>; GC does not scan loose mountpoint objects.
CAS exposes supportsTransactionalMutableFiles separately from append support because transactions rewrite txn_version.txt and do not require append.
Manifest backpressure delays writer-origin mutations between manifest_soft_limit and manifest_hard_limit and rejects mutations at or above the hard limit with LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Manifest staging enforces a maximum of 1,048,576 entries, 256 MiB encoded size, 16 MiB total inline bytes, and 1 MiB per inline entry.
B172 proposes moving blob staging to S3 with server-side copy to remove the local scratch-directory requirement and avoid rereading local files on condemned displacement.
